title: A held attempt must not become a stall: nobody is told, and releasing it throws the work away
description:
A held attempt is CORRECT and must stay. What turns it into a stall is that
nobody is told, and that clearing it throws the work away.

## What happened

Running the ticks deletion epic through ticfac on herdr (run epic-pwp), the
machine went to sleep mid-response. The pane says it outright: "API Error: Your
computer went to sleep mid-response." The worker had committed a476c6ea — a
clean extraction of the herdr socket client into internal/herdclient, ~1000
lines over 9 files, WHICH BUILDS — and was killed before writing RESULT-nkf.md.

Everything downstream was right: no report means no verdict, so collect refused
it, the run stopped rather than integrating an unproven change, the branch was
kept because those commits are the only copy, and the closed tick stayed closed.

Then it sat. That is the stall, and neither half of it is the hold's fault.

## 1. Nothing consumes the run feed

The feed says `run_finished: failed … nkf did not pass`. Nothing reads it, so no
one learns the run needs a person. The operator noticed by looking.

Tick u9l built the feed for exactly this and stopped at emitting it. Finish the
job: something that watches a run and surfaces a terminal-with-a-hold to a
human. It does not need to be clever — a held attempt is rare and important, and
the whole point is that the run cannot proceed without a decision.

## 2. Releasing a held attempt throws its work away

`ticfac settle --release` dispatches a NEW attempt and, in its own words,
"whatever the released attempt committed stays on its own write ref". So the
operator's choice today is: strand a thousand lines of good work, or hand-merge
a branch that never passed a gate.

That is why the hold is expensive, and an expensive decision is a decision that
waits. Add the third option the situation actually needs: release the attempt
AND base the next one on its branch, so the next worker starts from the work
rather than redoing it. The gate still decides — nothing merges unproven — but
the evidence the previous attempt produced is not thrown away because its
author was interrupted.

Design question this tick must answer: what does a resumed-from-work attempt
record in its provenance, so "this work came from a released attempt" survives?

## Not in scope, but say it in the doc

The machine sleeping mid-run is an operational hazard, not a ticfac bug. A long
run wants `caffeinate` or the equivalent. Worth one line where run-epic is
documented, because the failure it produces looks like a worker defect.

acceptance_criteria: A run that ends holding an attempt surfaces that to a human rather than only to the feed, and what surfaces says which tick and why; releasing a held attempt can carry its commits forward so the next attempt starts from them, with the gate still deciding and provenance recording that the work came from a released attempt; the operational hazard (a sleeping machine looks like a worker defect) is stated where run-epic is documented; tests cover a release that carries work and one that does not.
